history.summary: TOWN CORRECTED: the temple is not in Durg city but at Deorbija (Devarbija) village, Saja tehsil, Durg district — note some gazetteers now place the village in Bemetara district, and village coordinates conflict across sources (verify). The only evidence of the village's antiquity is this 12th-13th century CE sandstone temple on the western bank of the Devaraha tank. Dedicated to Shiva, it later received a female deity statue in the garbha-grha and came to be called the Sita Temple. It faces east with garbha-grha and antarala (the ardha-mandapa is lost), built in sapta-ratha plan with a nagara latina shikhara of seven bhumis; carvings include a rare Pandava-Shivalinga-worship scene on the antarala lintel (paralleled at Janjgir, Gandai and Ratanpur), Ganga-Yamuna door jambs, and bhadra-niche images of Natesa, Andhakantaka, Surya, Harihara-Hiranyagarbha, Mahishasuramardini, Vaishnavi and Kaumari. Local legend says it was built in six nights, and that Rama, Sita and Lakshmana visited during exile. It is a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India. Coordinates are approximate for the village (postal-code level; conflicting figures 21.2134/81.3854 vs 21.6667/81.4000 across gazetteers — verify).

name: Deorbijia Temple
town_description: Deorbijia (also spelled Deorbija or Devarbija) is a small village in Saja tehsil, historically of Durg district, Chhattisgarh, with postal code 491993. It lies on the Raipur-Bemetara road and is known almost entirely for its 12th-13th century sandstone temple on the Devaraha tank, a protected monument that draws heritage visitors and pilgrims.

travel.airport: Swami Vivekananda Airport, Raipur, about 60-70 km (verify)
travel.railway: Gundardehi is the nearest rail point per postal gazetteers; Raipur Junction is the major station, about 60 km (verify)
travel.road: On the Raipur-Bemetara road; hire a taxi from Raipur, Durg or Bemetara as public transport is limited (verify)
